trace.final_message:
Added `find_gaps` in `hourglass/gaps.py`, with tests, and committed it as `0d97d18`.

- **Behavior:** `find_gaps(worked, opening)` returns one label per uncovered stretch of opening hours, such as `gap 12:00-13:00 (sixty min)` (written with digits in the real output). Overlapping or unordered spans are fine. Touching spans leave no gap.
- **Out-of-hours spans:** a worked span that starts before opening or ends after closing raises `ValueError`. I picked `ValueError` because `Span` already uses it. `ProjectError` is documented for unusable schedule files, so it did not fit.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_gaps.py` has seven cases. They cover a gap in the middle, gaps at both ends, no spans, full coverage, overlap and order, and a span before opening and one after closing. The full suite passes with thirty-three tests, and the lint script reports no syntax errors.
- **Docs and exports:** I added a line to `docs/api.txt` and an entry to `CHANGES.txt`. I did not export `find_gaps` from `hourglass/__init__.py`, so import it from `hourglass.gaps`.
- **Style rules:** the new code follows the CLAUDE.md rules, so functions are at most eight lines and lines are at most sixty characters. Because of the one-blank-line rule, functions are separated by a single blank line, not the usual two.

I ran `git diff` before the commit, as the project notes require.

## Unreleased

before.docs/api.txt:
hourglass.parsing.parse_clock(text): read a clock time as minutes since midnight
hourglass.parsing.format_clock(minutes): minutes since midnight as HH:MM
hourglass.parsing.parse_span(text): read a range such as 09:00-17:30
hourglass.parsing.format_span(span): a span as start-end text
hourglass.parsing.normalize_day(text): short lowercase day name
hourglass.merging.spans_overlap(first, second): whether two spans share any time
hourglass.merging.intersect_spans(first, second): the part two spans share
hourglass.merging.merge_spans(spans): collapse overlaps into a sorted list
hourglass.merging.total_minutes(spans): minutes covered, overlaps counted once
hourglass.schedule.parse_schedule_text(text): parse schedule CSV held in memory
hourglass.schedule.load_schedule(path): read a schedule CSV from disk
hourglass.schedule.shifts_for_worker(shifts, worker): all shifts for one worker
hourglass.schedule.worker_minutes(shifts): scheduled minutes per worker
hourglass.schedule.day_coverage(shifts, day): merged spans for a day
hourglass.schedule.format_day_line(shifts, day): one text line for a day
